authority: Curated by the PrismPath maintainers against SP 800-53 Rev 5.2.0 and limited to the AU and SI families. Ids use the OSCAL spelling, so au-9.3 is AU-9(3). The existing adapters/compliance/crosswalks/nist_800171_r2__nist_800_53_r5.json (NIST CPRT) maps 800-171 requirements onto the same control ids and is not repeated here.

edges.does_not_satisfy: AU-2 expects an organization defined event list and AU-3 expects the source and identity of the actor, and neither is settled by a receipt alone. AU-10 depends on the root statement and on who holds the instance key.
edges.rationale: Each decision is an auditable event the system generates (AU-2, AU-12). A receipt records what happened, the outcome, the time and the policy in force, which covers much of AU-3. With the signed root it supports non-repudiation (AU-10).

edges.does_not_satisfy: The instance key is on the deployment, so a party who controls the deployment controls the key. AU-9 also covers access control and backup of the log, which PrismPath does not provide.
edges.rationale: Signed, chained roots protect the audit information against modification and removal (AU-9, AU-9(3)), give attribution to a deployment key (AU-10) and are an integrity check over recorded information (SI-7).

edges.does_not_satisfy: The scope is the policy artifact. SI-7 across the rest of the system, and software supply chain controls outside the AU and SI families, are not addressed.
edges.rationale: The loader verifies integrity before use (SI-7, SI-7(1)), authenticates code with a signature (SI-7(15)), validates the structure of the image and rejects malformed input (SI-10) and names a signed fail-safe node (SI-17).

edges.does_not_satisfy: It runs when invoked and does not meet SI-6's schedule, transition or notification parameters on its own.
edges.rationale: The host records which verified image is in force and the delivery assessor re-runs the checks on a copy, which is a verification of a security function after delivery (SI-6).

edges.does_not_satisfy: It covers policy and flow artifacts at the loader and nothing else.
edges.rationale: A refusal of an older signed policy is an automated response to an integrity violation (SI-7(5)) and is written as an audit event whether it succeeds or is refused (AU-12).

edges.does_not_satisfy: Related controls sit in other families, such as access control, and are not mapped here.
edges.none: AU and SI hold no control for a human decision point.

edges.does_not_satisfy: Review, analysis and reporting are done by people or tools the operator runs. SI-4's monitoring objectives and AU-6's review frequency are the organization's.
edges.rationale: A frozen cause adds the reason to the audit record (AU-3), and counting by cause over the trail is an analysis input (AU-6, SI-4). A refusal names its cause without exposing internals (SI-11).

edges.does_not_satisfy: The actor is the interface and a session fingerprint, not an identified person, which leaves part of AU-3 open. The console is single user and local, so access control for the log (AU-9) and non-repudiation of the human are not met.
edges.rationale: Control actions are written as audit events before they act, and an action does not run when its intent cannot be written (AU-5, AU-12). Events are Merkle committed and, with an instance key, signed (AU-9). The auditing interface reads trails (AU-6).

edges.does_not_satisfy: AU-8 concerns the system's clock and time source for every record. An anchor times a root statement, not each receipt.
edges.rationale: An anchor gives a time for a root statement that does not depend on the deployment's own clock.
